boise.note: Agency source and satellite facility review completed 2026-10-29. Only sections with two documented access sites and a separate section approval are shown; approximate markers do not establish an exact landing or river path.

snake-sf-swan.note: Named public access and agency river-mile evidence reviewed 2026-11-03. Independently approved sections show maps with precision labels. Palisades Dam coordinate remains unresolved; existing approximate areas do not claim a surveyed landing.

snake-sf-canyon.note: Named public access and agency river-mile evidence reviewed 2026-11-03. Independently approved sections show maps with precision labels. Palisades Dam coordinate remains unresolved; existing approximate areas do not claim a surveyed landing.

teton.note: Named public facilities, published guide mileage and satellite imagery checked 2026-11-03. Individually reviewed maps show approximate access areas; exact shoreline pins and river-course geometry are reviewed separately.

henrys-fork-ashton.note: Named facilities, published guide distances and satellite imagery reviewed. Approved sections show approximate access areas; exact shoreline connections and route geometry are separate reviews.

henrys-fork-box.note: Named facilities, published guide distances and satellite imagery reviewed. Approved sections show approximate access areas; exact shoreline connections and route geometry are separate reviews.

henrys-fork-lower.note: Named facilities, published guide distances and satellite imagery reviewed. Approved sections show approximate access areas; exact shoreline connections and route geometry are separate reviews.

henrys-fork-big-springs.note: Public boating facilities and approximate areas reviewed separately from exact landings and river-course geometry. The spring-fed channel is incomplete in the current USGS route source.

payette-main.note: Public Payette boating facilities, guide distances and imagery reviewed. Individually approved sections show approximate access maps; ambiguous legacy endpoints remain pending.

payette-sf.note: Public Payette boating facilities, guide distances and imagery reviewed. Individually approved sections show approximate access maps; ambiguous legacy endpoints remain pending.

salmon-riggins.note: Official public boating access, named facility identities and approximate areas checked separately from river-course geometry. Approved sections have individual reviews; dotted lines require independent full-course checks.

salmon-salmon.note: Official public boating access, named facility identities and approximate areas checked separately from river-course geometry. Approved sections have individual reviews; dotted lines require independent full-course checks.

selway.note: Agency facility identities reviewed separately from exact shoreline pins and river geometry. Only individually approved sections show maps; unresolved trip definitions remain held.

lochsa.note: White Pine, Fish Creek and Knife Edge are documented public access areas. The Lowell entry remains held; Wild Goose is a separate seasonally closed facility, not a substitute Lowell pin. Only individually reviewed sections display maps.

Barber Park.directions: Use the signed public entrance and designated river access at Barber Park. Check the operator’s current hours and seasonal conditions before arranging the shuttle.
Barber Park.sourceName: City of Boise Fire Department Float the Boise public access map
Barber Park.note: The official public-access map identifies this designated landing; satellite review places it at the beach/stair access, not in a parking lot. Launch only during the official float season after the river is opened.

Ann Morrison Park.directions: Use the signed public entrance and designated river access at Ann Morrison Park. Check the operator’s current hours and seasonal conditions before arranging the shuttle.
Ann Morrison Park.sourceName: City of Boise Fire Department Float the Boise public access map
Ann Morrison Park.note: The official public-access map identifies this designated landing; satellite review places it at the beach/stair access, not in a parking lot. All floaters must exit at Ann Morrison Park; the diversion dam downstream is dangerous.
Ann Morrison Park.bankSourceName: Ada County Parks & Waterways — Float the Boise guide (2025)
Ann Morrison Park.bankNote: The agency guide explicitly places the Ann Morrison takeout on river left, facing downstream. This agrees with the reviewed official takeout feature and satellite placement.

Eagle Island.note: No sourced access record has been added yet.

Orofino.note: The BLM Clearwater guide lists Orofino City Park as foot access without a boat-ramp or canoe-launch designation. A named public boating landing for this Orofino endpoint remains unconfirmed; a town or park coordinate alone is insufficient.

Peck.note: The BLM Clearwater guide lists Peck Sports Access as foot access without a boat-ramp or canoe-launch designation. Confirm a public boating landing and lawful approach before using this endpoint; do not substitute nearby Harpers Bend without reviewing the trip.

Spalding (Nez Perce NHP).note: The BLM guide lists the Spalding pulloff as foot access. A public boat takeout and carrying route through the park remain unconfirmed. The NPS compendium limits pedestrian travel to designated paths and mown areas; a park coordinate does not establish a boat landing.

Warm River Campground.note: HFF lower-river access guide, page 6, lists this as wading access without a boat ramp. Stone Bridge is a separate documented boat launch; do not move this campground identity to that launch.

Ashton (Vernon area).note: This legacy name combines distinct locations on opposite sides of Ashton Dam. Use the separately named Ashton Reservoir Boat Ramp or Vernon Bridge; no dependable single landing matches this label.

areaCenter.feature: Vernon boat-access staging area

Vernon Bridge.directions: Use the designated Vernon access and ramp, not an arbitrary point in St. Anthony. Chester Dam is downstream; a trip continuing past it requires separately confirmed takeout, portage and relaunch arrangements.
Vernon Bridge.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Vernon Bridge.note: IDFG and HFF lower guide, page 26, identify Vernon as a boating facility. The agency coordinate lies back from the river in the staging area. Access review does not approve the old Vernon-to-St-Anthony itinerary.

St. Anthony.note: The city name does not identify a specific landing. HFF lists multiple distinct sites with differing boat access. A precise facility and the Chester Dam crossing must be resolved for the legacy Vernon itinerary.

areaCenter.feature: Box Canyon launch parking and staging area

Island Park Dam (Box Canyon).accessType: Public boat ramp below Island Park Dam
Island Park Dam (Box Canyon).directions: Use the Box Canyon boat ramp BELOW Island Park Dam, not a ramp on Island Park Reservoir or the hike-in campground access. Identify the ramp from the parking area before unloading.
Island Park Dam (Box Canyon).sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Island Park Dam (Box Canyon).note: IDFG point is in the parking loop, set back from the ramp. The HFF upper-river guide, page 45, and USFS boat-ramp inventory independently identify this below-dam boating access.

areaCenter.feature: Last Chance boat-access parking area

Last Chance.directions: Use the signed Last Chance boat ramp and designated day-use parking. Confirm this takeout before launching from Box Canyon; the marker identifies the facility rather than the exact shoreline landing.
Last Chance.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Last Chance.note: IDFG point lies in parking near the bank, consistent with the HFF upper-river guide, page 52. It does not establish the water-edge ramp position.

White Pine / Knife Blade.note: Retired ambiguous identity retained for historical reports. It combined White Pine upstream of Fish Creek with Knife Edge downstream. The corrected White Pine–Fish Creek section uses the separate White Pine River Access ID; Knife Edge has its own ID and section. Do not assign a coordinate to this combined label.

Fish Creek.note: USFS boating-site record 5217.000411 identifies this facility, distinct from Fish Creek Trailhead and unrelated Fish Creek campgrounds. Approximate access area only; no exact landing or bank-side instruction.

areaCenter.feature: USFS public boating facility vicinity; approximate area, not a surveyed landing

Fish Creek.sourceName: US Forest Service recreation site inventory
Fish Creek.directions: Use the signed Fish Creek River Access on Highway 12 beside the Lochsa River. USFS documents stairs and a raft slide; confirm the usable water entry and parking on arrival.

Wilderness Gateway.note: USFS and Recreation.gov document direct Lochsa River access and rafting here. The inventory coordinate is within the campground. It is not the separate North Wilderness Gateway staging area in the emergency-response plan, and no driving or shore connector is mapped.

areaCenter.feature: USFS public boating facility vicinity; approximate area, not a surveyed landing

Wilderness Gateway.sourceName: US Forest Service recreation site inventory
Wilderness Gateway.directions: Use the designated river access at Wilderness Gateway Campground on Highway 12. Confirm the usable launch and parking at the facility before your shuttle; the marker identifies the campground access area, not an exact shore entry.

Lowell.note: A town/confluence label is not yet a documented public takeout. The Three Rivers Lodge response-plan coordinate is a water intake, not a boat launch; it must not become an access pin. Check a named public boating facility before promoting this identity.

Banks.note: USFS and the BLM boating guide identify this public launch. The pin is the agency facility area beside the parking loop, not an exact water-entry point. USFS lists a late-May through late-September operating season, subject to snow; confirm current access and fees before arranging a shuttle.

areaCenter.feature: USFS boating-facility inventory; approximate access area, not a surveyed shoreline landing

Banks.sourceName: Boise National Forest facility page and Payette River boating guide
Banks.directions: Use the signed Banks River Access at the Highway 55/Banks-Lowman Road junction. The marker identifies the public boating facility, not Banks Beach farther downstream or the nearby store. Use the signed ramp and keep the loading area clear.

Beehive Bend.note: BLM identifies Beehive Bend as the Main Payette takeout. Approximate facility area only; no shoreline or driving connector is mapped. Day use only. The current BLM page lists $5 daily parking or the $30 Boise National Forest Annual Day Use Pass; confirm posted fees when visiting.

areaCenter.feature: BLM boating-facility inventory; approximate access area, not a surveyed shoreline landing

Beehive Bend.sourceName: Bureau of Land Management facility page and Payette River boating guide
Beehive Bend.directions: Use the signed Beehive Bend takeout on Highway 55, about six miles north of Horseshoe Bend. The pin marks the facility entrance/parking vicinity. Follow the signed path to the river and confirm the usable landing before launching upstream.

Horseshoe Bend boat ramp.note: No sourced access record has been added yet.

Cabarton Bridge.note: No sourced access record has been added yet.

Kirkham / Lowman.note: No sourced access record has been added yet.

Deadwood Campground.note: No sourced access record has been added yet.

Danskin.note: USFS site 5531.002731 and BLM guide SF04 identify the South Fork Payette launch. The marker is an approximate facility area inland of the river, not an exact landing. Day use only; USFS lists late May through late September, subject to snow. The separate South Fork Boise site is not part of this trip.

areaCenter.feature: USFS boating-facility inventory; approximate access area, not a surveyed shoreline landing

Danskin.sourceName: Boise National Forest facility page and Payette River boating guide
Danskin.directions: Use Danskin Rest Area Boating Site beside the South Fork Payette on Banks-Lowman Road. This is not Danskin Floatboat Access on the South Fork Boise River. Use the signed public facility and check seasonal access before setting a shuttle.

Confluence (Garden Valley).note: BLM documents a gravel ramp and parking at this takeout. The marker uses its approximate facility-area coordinate; no exact landing or shore connector is claimed. Day use only. The current BLM page lists $5 daily parking or the $30 Boise National Forest Annual Day Use Pass; check posted fees and conditions.

areaCenter.feature: BLM boating-facility inventory; approximate access area, not a surveyed shoreline landing

Confluence (Garden Valley).sourceName: Bureau of Land Management facility page and Payette River boating guide
Confluence (Garden Valley).directions: Use the BLM Confluence boating site on Banks-Lowman Road just downstream of the Middle Fork/South Fork Payette junction. This is the Garden Valley takeout, not the North Fork confluence at Banks. Finish here; continuing downstream enters the harder Staircase run.

Riggins city.note: Approximate launch area derived from the boat-launch symbol on BLM’s April 2026 georeferenced river map and checked against imagery. The symbol spans roughly 100 metres at map scale; this is not an exact shoreline or bank-side instruction.

areaCenter.feature: BLM 2026 boat-launch map symbol; approximate access area, not a surveyed shoreline landing

Riggins city.sourceName: BLM Lower Salmon boating map and guide
Riggins city.directions: Use the signed City of Riggins boat launch beside the city park. This is not Shorts Bar or Island Bar upstream. Confirm the usable ramp and parking when setting your shuttle.

Lucile.note: BLM identifies this as a Riggins-trip takeout. Its facility GIS point and current river-map symbol agree on this site; the general web-page coordinate points farther downstream and was not adopted. The marker is an approximate facility area. Day use only; no camping.

areaCenter.feature: Agency boating-facility inventory; approximate access area, not a surveyed shoreline landing

Lucile.sourceName: BLM Lucile boating facility and GIS inventory
Lucile.directions: Use Lucile Recreation Site off Highway 95 near milepost 203.8. This is the developed parking and launch site downstream of Old Lucile; the two launches are separate.

Hammer Creek.note: BLM documents public boating access here. The approximate area comes from the launch symbol on BLM’s April 2026 georeferenced map, checked against imagery. It is about 160 metres south of the recreation-inventory center; the latter was not used as a launch pin. No exact landing or shore connector is claimed. Camping fees and current Lower Salmon permit/equipment rules apply.

areaCenter.feature: BLM 2026 boat-launch map symbol; approximate access area, not a surveyed shoreline landing

Hammer Creek.sourceName: BLM Lower Salmon boating map and guide
Hammer Creek.directions: Use the signed Hammer Creek Recreation Site boat launch west of White Bird. Follow the facility signs from the road to the ramp; the marker identifies the approximate launch area.

Heller Bar (Snake confluence).note: Legacy duplicate label, retained for identity history only. The actual Heller Bar concrete ramp is the existing Washington record acc-2aefb784ba22590db8e8, downstream of the Grande Ronde confluence on the Snake. It is not at the Salmon/Snake confluence. Do not independently promote or create a second landing here.

Salmon (Island Park ramp).note: IDFG site 264 identifies this City of Salmon facility with two boat ramps. The agency coordinate marks the park/ramp vicinity, not a specific shoreline entry. The park is open 6 a.m.–10 p.m.; IDFG lists running-water restrooms March 1–November 30. No camping.

areaCenter.feature: Agency boating-facility inventory; approximate access area, not a surveyed shoreline landing

Salmon (Island Park ramp).sourceName: Idaho Fish and Game public boating access inventory
Salmon (Island Park ramp).directions: Use City of Salmon Island Park and its designated boat ramps. This is Island Park in Lemhi County, not Island Park Reservoir in Fremont County. Confirm the suitable ramp and parking at the park.

North Fork.note: IDFG site 295 lists an active boat ramp and a public-access lease at North Fork. Approximate facility area only. Daylight use only; adjacent campsites and picnic sites are private. This is North Fork on the upper Salmon, not the remote Middle Fork confluence.

areaCenter.feature: Agency boating-facility inventory; approximate access area, not a surveyed shoreline landing

North Fork.operator: Idaho Fish and Game / private access lease
North Fork.sourceName: Idaho Fish and Game public boating access inventory
North Fork.directions: Use the designated North Fork boat access behind the North Fork Store and Campground off US Highway 93. This public access is provided through an Idaho Fish and Game/private land lease. Stay within the signed access area.

Paradise Guard Station.note: USFS identifies this developed boat launch separately from Paradise Campground, about half a mile away. The marker is an approximate launch area. No overnight parking at the launch; the Forest Service directs overnight parking east of Paradise Campground. No drinking water.

areaCenter.feature: USFS public boating facility vicinity; approximate area, not a surveyed landing

Paradise Guard Station.sourceName: US Forest Service recreation site inventory
Paradise Guard Station.directions: Use Paradise Boating Site at the end of Forest Road 6223, reached from Magruder Crossing. Follow the launch signs rather than stopping at the campground. Check mountain-road conditions before arranging the long shuttle.

Race Creek / Selway Falls.note: USFS boating-site record 6974.000961 identifies Race Track as the wilderness-trip takeout above Selway Falls. This is an approximate cobble-bar access area, distinct from Race Creek Campground farther upstream. No amenities or mapped shore connection. The falls are outside this trip.

areaCenter.feature: USFS public boating facility vicinity; approximate area, not a surveyed landing

Race Creek / Selway Falls.sourceName: US Forest Service recreation site inventory
Race Creek / Selway Falls.directions: Use the Race Track wilderness takeout on Selway River Road 223, approximately 20 road miles upstream from Lowell. It is above Selway Falls. Identify the cobble-bar takeout while setting your shuttle and take out before the falls.

Conant.operator: Bureau of Land Management — Upper Snake Field Office
Conant.directions: Follow Conant Valley Loop to the signed Conant boat access. Concrete-boat and raft launch areas are separate. Confirm your chosen launch or takeout and use the designated parking.
Conant.sourceName: BLM — South Fork Snake public access and boating regulations
Conant.note: BLM public GIS identifies the Conant facility at the parking/staging area. Imagery and BLM river-mile map agree on this location. Reject the visit-page coordinate near Spring Creek; do not snap this staging point to a guessed shoreline landing.

areaCenter.feature: Conant boat-access staging and parking area

Byington.operator: Bureau of Land Management — Upper Snake Field Office
Byington.directions: Follow the signed Byington boat-access road from the Swan Valley Highway. Use the designated concrete ramp or separate raft facility and arrange a shuttle before launching.
Byington.sourceName: BLM — South Fork Snake public access and boating regulations
Byington.note: BLM public GIS point lies on the concrete ramp apron in imagery; the agency visit page confirms a concrete ramp and separate raft facilities. This identifies the ramp, not a surveyed seasonal water edge.

Lorenzo.operator: Bureau of Land Management — Upper Snake Field Office
Lorenzo.directions: Use the signed Lorenzo boat access from the Menan exit on US 20. The marker locates the riverside parking area; identify the concrete ramp before starting your float.
Lorenzo.sourceName: BLM — South Fork Snake public access and boating regulations
Lorenzo.note: BLM public GIS point lies in the riverside parking area near the ramp. Retain as an approximate facility location rather than calling the parking point an exact takeout.

areaCenter.feature: Lorenzo boat-access parking beside the river

Palisades Dam.note: BLM map 1 locates the named boat access beside the paved loop below the dam; satellite imagery corroborates the ramp and road layout. The marker represents that approximate access area, not a surveyed landing. The Forest Service web/GIS coordinate points far east of the dam and is not used. Help refine the marker through the correction link if you know the landing.
Palisades Dam.operator: U.S. Forest Service — Caribou-Targhee National Forest
Palisades Dam.sourceName: USFS — Palisades Dam Boat Landing; BLM — South Fork Snake boating map 1

areaCenter.feature: Approximate below-dam boat-access area interpreted from BLM map 1 and checked against imagery; not an agency GPS fix

Palisades Dam.directions: Follow the signed Palisades Dam boat access below the dam via Riverside Parkway. Confirm the usable ramp and takeout while setting your shuttle. This is the river launch, not Calamity on the reservoir or Palisades Creek.

Spring Creek.operator: U.S. Forest Service — Caribou-Targhee National Forest
Spring Creek.directions: Use the signed Spring Creek boat access at the Swan Valley Highway bridge. The marker is the Forest Service facility point; confirm the concrete ramp and exit before launching.
Spring Creek.sourceName: BLM — South Fork Snake public access and boating regulations
Spring Creek.note: USFS facility point lies near the river bank, away from the visible ramp. BLM map 4 independently identifies Spring Creek beside the highway bridge. Retain as an approximate area; do not confuse it with Conant two river miles downstream.

areaCenter.feature: Spring Creek boating facility below the Swan Valley highway bridge

Avery.note: No sourced access record has been added yet.

Calder.note: No sourced access record has been added yet.

St. Maries.note: No sourced access record has been added yet.

areaCenter.feature: Buxton River Park / Bates Bridge access area

Bates Bridge.accessType: Public boat ramp at Buxton River Park
Bates Bridge.operator: Idaho Department of Fish and Game / Teton County public access
Bates Bridge.directions: Use Buxton River Park on the NORTH side of Bates Road. The old south-side access was decommissioned. Use the park entrance and designated ramp and parking; do not stop on the road at the area marker.
Bates Bridge.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Bates Bridge.note: FTR project documentation confirms the modern north-side access and decommissioned south-side landing. Imagery agrees. IDFG point falls near the road at the facility, not on the ramp; retain it only as an approximate area.

areaCenter.feature: Rainey / Big Eddy parking and river access

Rainey Bridge.operator: Idaho Department of Fish and Game / Teton County public access
Rainey Bridge.directions: Use the Rainey access, also called Big Eddy. The marker is the facility parking/staging area near the gravel ramp. Check the access road before setting your shuttle; IDFG warns it can be slick when wet or snowy.
Rainey Bridge.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Rainey Bridge.note: Agency point is in parking south of the visible river entry. The recreation map independently identifies Rainey/Big Eddy. This is not an exact landing or a claim that a bridge is present.

areaCenter.feature: Cache / Packsaddle Bridge access and parking

Cache Bridge.operator: Idaho Department of Fish and Game / Teton County public access
Cache Bridge.directions: Use the designated access at Packsaddle Bridge on Packsaddle Road, also called Cache Bridge. Identify the ramp and use the marked parking; the area marker sits beside the river rather than at the exact landing.
Cache Bridge.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Cache Bridge.note: Agency coordinate falls in the access apron beside Packsaddle Bridge. The recreation map confirms Cache as its alternate name. Preserve approximate precision.

Smiths Ferry (Cabarton takeout).note: BLM NF02 identifies the Smiths Ferry takeout as private. Confirm current access arrangements and exact landing before placing a map pin.

Fullmer.operator: U.S. Forest Service — Caribou-Targhee National Forest
Fullmer.directions: Use the signed Fullmer Boat Landing and confirm road conditions and the shuttle before launching. The marker locates the parking area above the concrete river ramp.
Fullmer.sourceName: BLM — South Fork Snake public access and boating regulations
Fullmer.note: USFS point falls at the parking area above the visible ramp, not at the water. BLM lists this public intermediate access at river mile 28. Exact shoreline location remains unconfirmed.

areaCenter.feature: Fullmer boat-access parking and approach
Fox Creek West access and approach

Fox Creek West.operator: Idaho Department of Fish and Game / Teton County public access
Fox Creek West.directions: Use the designated Fox Creek West access reached from the west side of the valley. IDFG lists a gravel boat ramp and day use only. Confirm the river approach before launching; the marker identifies the access area.
Fox Creek West.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Fox Creek West.note: Agency point is on the access approach, set back from the river. Preserve the sourced area location rather than snapping it to water.

areaCenter.feature: Fox Creek East parking and walk-in approach

Fox Creek East.accessType: Public carry-in river access; no listed boat ramp
Fox Creek East.operator: Idaho Department of Fish and Game / Teton County public access
Fox Creek East.directions: Use the designated Fox Creek East access at the end of the access road. Plan to carry your craft to the river; IDFG lists no developed boat ramp. Inspect the carrying route and arrange your shuttle before unloading.
Fox Creek East.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Fox Creek East.note: The guide lists this as a float access, but IDFG lists fishing access without a ramp. Imagery shows parking well back from the river and a foot approach. Keep it approximate and do not imply trailer access.

areaCenter.feature: South Bates / Nickerson access beside the bridge

South Bates Bridge.operator: Idaho Department of Fish and Game / Teton County public access
South Bates Bridge.directions: Use the signed public access at South Bates Bridge, also called Nickerson and listed by IDFG as Teton Creek. Parking is limited. Identify the river entry and your shuttle arrangement before launching.
South Bates Bridge.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
South Bates Bridge.note: Agency Teton Creek point matches the South Bates/Nickerson site on the recreation map. It lies in the access area near the bridge, not at the water edge.

areaCenter.feature: Horseshoe access at the end of Old Rightaway Road

Horseshoe Bridge.accessType: Public river access; developed ramp unconfirmed
Horseshoe Bridge.operator: Idaho Department of Fish and Game / Teton County public access
Horseshoe Bridge.directions: Use the designated Horseshoe access at Old Rightaway Road. Confirm the bank and carrying approach before your trip. IDFG does not list a developed boat ramp here; do not assume trailer access or an intact road bridge.
Horseshoe Bridge.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Horseshoe Bridge.note: The recreation guide lists Horseshoe as a float endpoint, while current IDFG inventory lists fishing access with no ramp. The point is at the clearing beside the river. Show the facility area without certifying ramp suitability.

areaCenter.feature: Harrops Bridge boat-access staging area

Harrops Bridge.operator: Idaho Department of Fish and Game / Teton County public access
Harrops Bridge.directions: Use the designated Harrops Bridge gravel-ramp access at Highway 33. Identify the takeout before launching. End meadow-water floats here: the downstream canyon is technical whitewater, not a continuation of this easy reach.
Harrops Bridge.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Harrops Bridge.note: Agency point lies in the small staging area beside the ramp and bridge. The recreation guide identifies Harrops as the end of the upper meadow floats. Keep it an approximate facility point, not an exact shoreline pin.

areaCenter.feature: Stone Bridge launch apron beside the Henrys Fork

Stone Bridge.directions: Use the designated Stone Bridge launch on the Henrys Fork by the road bridge, below the Warm River confluence. This is a different access from Warm River Campground. Use the launch parking and confirm the ramp before starting.
Stone Bridge.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Stone Bridge.note: IDFG identifies Stone Bridge and a separate Warm River ADA point at nearly the same apron. HFF lower guide, page 8, identifies the boat launch. Preserve one boating-facility identity rather than duplicating the adjacent ADA feature.

areaCenter.feature: Jump Off Canyon access apron on Fishermans Drive

Jump Off Canyon.directions: Use the designated Jump Off Canyon river access along Fishermans Drive. Identify the ramp beside the parking apron and arrange a shuttle before launching. This is the upstream alternative to the Ashton Reservoir ramp.
Jump Off Canyon.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Jump Off Canyon.note: IDFG coordinate is on the roadside parking apron, not at the ramp. HFF lower guide, page 11, confirms this named boat access and its one-mile connection to Ashton Reservoir.

areaCenter.feature: Ashton Reservoir ramp staging area

Ashton Reservoir Boat Ramp.directions: Use the Ashton Reservoir recreation-area boat ramp near the upper end of the reservoir. This takeout is ABOVE Ashton Dam and is not Vernon Bridge below the dam. Set the shuttle here and take out at this facility.
Ashton Reservoir Boat Ramp.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Ashton Reservoir Boat Ramp.note: IDFG coordinate is above the paved ramp in its staging area. HFF lower guide, page 14, names the facility; PacifiCorp also identifies the reservoir ramp as the takeout for upstream floats. Do not place a takeout at Ashton Dam.

areaCenter.feature: Red Road Bridge access approach near the ramp

Red Road Bridge.directions: Use the signed Red Road Bridge boat access off the Salem/Parker Highway. Follow the designated access drive to the ramp and parking instead of stopping on the highway. The marker is near the ramp approach, not an exact landing.
Red Road Bridge.note: BLM ramp-specific inventory is closer to the ramp than IDFG’s general entrance point. Imagery shows it beside the approach, still set back from the water. BLM’s visit page and HFF lower guide, page 52, independently confirm boating access.

areaCenter.feature: Warm Slough boat-access staging area

Warm Slough.operator: Idaho Department of Fish and Game
Warm Slough.directions: Use the designated Warm Slough boating access and identify its ramp before launching. This facility is on a river branch; check the actual channel and landing approach when arranging your shuttle.
Warm Slough.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Warm Slough.note: IDFG point lies in the access area beside the ramp. HFF lower guide, page 56, and BLM confirm this facility. Keep the source location approximate; it does not identify which changing channel to navigate.

areaCenter.feature: Beaver Dick Park boat-access area

Beaver Dick Park.directions: Use the designated boat ramp at Beaver Dick Park beside Highway 33. Identify the ramp and park entrance while setting your shuttle; the area marker is near the bank but is not an exact water-edge pin.
Beaver Dick Park.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Beaver Dick Park.note: IDFG point lies beside the ramp apron, consistent with the HFF lower guide, page 59, and BLM facility list. Preserve the approximate facility position rather than claiming surveyed landing precision.

areaCenter.feature: Agency-listed boating facility approach

Big Springs Water Trail Launch.directions: Use the designated water-trail launch beside the old railroad trestle, downstream of the springs viewing area. Carry light boats to the dock/stairs; there is no trailer ramp. Keep the unloading area clear and use designated parking.
Big Springs Water Trail Launch.sourceName: U.S. Forest Service — public boating-site inventory
Big Springs Water Trail Launch.note: The Forest Service boating-site point identifies the trestle-side approach. The USFS recreation guide and HFF study identify a hand-carry launch here. The shoreline connection is not surveyed.

areaCenter.feature: Designated public takeout clearing shown in HFF/USFS field-study Figure 3

Big Springs Water Trail Public Takeout.directions: Use the designated Forest Service clearing on the north side of the river, about half a mile upstream of the Highway 20 bridge. Reach it by the signed access road and confirm parking while setting your shuttle. Nearby cabin docks and the private bridge-side landings are separate facilities.
Big Springs Water Trail Public Takeout.sourceName: Henry’s Fork Foundation / Caribou-Targhee National Forest — water-trail field study, Figure 3
Big Springs Water Trail Public Takeout.note: The HFF/Caribou-Targhee field study, Figure 3 on page 8, identifies the public clearing. The USFS facility coordinate is about 90 m east near cabins, so this approximate area center was placed in the depicted clearing using satellite imagery. Original agency geometry is preserved in the review binding; this is not an exact landing fix.

areaCenter.feature: Ora Bridge ramp approach from HFF lower-river access guide, page 23

Ora Bridge.directions: Use the Ora Bridge ramp downstream of the road bridge, reached through the designated access drive and parking on the south side of the road. This is below Ashton Dam. Set your takeout at Vernon Bridge before launching.
Ora Bridge.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Ora Bridge.note: IDFG confirms active non-motorized boating access but its general point lies across the road from the launch. The HFF lower-river guide, page 23, supplies a ramp-area coordinate that matches the visible access apron below the bridge. Use that source-backed approximate area; no surveyed shoreline fix is claimed.

areaCenter.feature: Upper ramp approach beside Chester Dam

Chester Dam Upstream Ramp.directions: Use the designated ramp above Chester Dam for floats arriving from Ora or Vernon. Identify the upper ramp while setting your shuttle; the separate ramp below the powerhouse is not the takeout for this reach. Do not continue over the dam.
Chester Dam Upstream Ramp.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Chester Dam Upstream Ramp.note: IDFG lists the boating facility; the HFF guide identifies separate ramps above and below the dam. This agency point falls in the upper parking/ramp approach. It identifies an approximate access area, not a surveyed shoreline landing.

areaCenter.feature: Separate downstream launch apron below the powerhouse

Chester Dam Downstream Ramp.directions: Use the separate launch apron below the Chester Dam powerhouse. Confirm the downstream ramp and your Fun Farm takeout before launching. This itinerary starts below the dam; it does not include a dam crossing or portage from the upstream ramp.
Chester Dam Downstream Ramp.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Chester Dam Downstream Ramp.note: IDFG uses one general facility point for Chester. HFF pages 29–32 identify and illustrate distinct upper and lower ramps. Satellite imagery places this approximate area at the lower apron below the powerhouse; the original agency point is preserved in the binding. No exact landing fix is claimed.

areaCenter.feature: Fun Farm takeout apron upstream of the bridge

Fun Farm Bridge.directions: Use the designated Fun Farm boating takeout upstream of the road bridge. Check the ramp and current signs while setting your shuttle; do not continue to the diversion dam downstream. The bridge has been replaced, so older photographs may look different.
Fun Farm Bridge.sourceName: IDFG — public fishing and boating access inventory
Fun Farm Bridge.note: IDFG currently lists a boating ramp. HFF page 36 identifies the county takeout. The general agency point is in the parking area; this approximate center is at the visible ramp approach. Bridge-replacement imagery is not a current ramp-condition inspection, and the exact shoreline connection remains unverified.

areaCenter.feature: USFS public river-access facility vicinity; approximate, not a surveyed landing

White Pine River Access.directions: Use the signed White Pine River Access, also called Indian Grave Creek, near Highway 12 milepost 138. A primitive gravel drive leads to the loading area; unload one group at a time and use the small parking area above it.
White Pine River Access.note: The current Forest Service page documents public kayak and canoe access, limited parking and no camping. The USFS inventory coordinate is represented as an approximate facility area, not an exact ramp or bank-side instruction. White Pine and Knife Edge are separate sites.

areaCenter.feature: USFS public river-access facility vicinity; approximate, not a surveyed landing

Knife Edge River Access.directions: Use Knife Edge Campground and River Access on Highway 12, about 11.6 road miles east of Lowell. Identify the usable landing and parking before setting the shuttle. Snow can restrict access.
Knife Edge River Access.note: USFS identifies this public river/boat access separately from White Pine. The inventory coordinate is an approximate facility area, not a surveyed landing. A 2026 order reserved some campsites for boating-season parking through June 30; it did not close the river access. Check current notices before visiting.
